title: DriveSceneGen: Generating Diverse and Realistic Driving Scenarios From Scratch

control_signal.value: No user-specified control signal; scenarios are sampled from Gaussian noise. Diversity comes from sampling and from K multi-modal futures predicted per generated initial scene.

control_mechanism.value: Not a control mechanism: unconditional DDPM generates a rasterized BEV initial scene (map plus agent states), vectorized by a graph method; a trajectory prediction model then rolls out futures.

base_model.value: DDPM with U-Net backbone (four down/up blocks, self-attention middle block, 56M parameters) for BEV scene generation; graph-based vectorization; repurposed MTR for simulation stage.

datasets.value: Waymo Motion dataset, 70k scenarios of 20 seconds; 5k generated scenarios evaluated against it.

metrics.value: FID for fidelity; average feature distance for diversity (discrepancy vs ground truth in percent); vectorization GEO and TOPO precision, recall, F1.

controllability_evidence.value: No controllability experiment. Closest evidence is distribution matching: map plus agent initial states at 80m give FID 46.81 and diversity discrepancy 1.25%; same initial scene yields distinct futures qualitatively.

stated_limitations.value: Whole-scenario generation is a new task with no quantitative metric yet to compare generated dynamic scenarios against the ground-truth distribution; authors plan to investigate such metrics.

notes: Not really about controllable generation; unconditional from-scratch generator. Packet does not discuss other limitations.
